text:
anya: Quick smoke summary — small-batch (batch=1, seq~64) quantization sweep across H100 (us-west), A100 (eu-west), and A100 (ap-southeast). Sending raw numbers + takeaways.

matt: Nice, post the perf table and quality deltas please.

anya: paste:
```
CONFIG: model=marlin-70b, prompt-suite=prod-qa-1k, batch=1, seq=64, reps=3
Targets: p50 latency, p99 latency, tokens/sec (small-batch), QA_acc (EM %), perf/quality tradeoff
```

anya: H100 (us-west)
- FP16: p50=78ms, p99=210ms, tkn/s=18.5, QA_acc=86.9% (baseline)
- BF16: p50=80ms, p99=215ms, tkn/s=18.0, QA_acc=86.9% (no diff)
- INT8 (fast_int8_v2): p50=42ms, p99=170ms, tkn/s=34.7, QA_acc=85.1% (Δ=-1.8%) -> 2.0x p50 speedup
- FP8 (ef32-quant): p50=54ms, p99=185ms, tkn/s=26.8, QA_acc=86.5% (Δ=-0.4%) -> 1.45x p50 speedup

anya: A100 (eu-west)
- FP16: p50=95ms, p99=240ms, tkn/s=15.6, QA_acc=86.9% (baseline)
- INT8 (fast_int8_v2): p50=70ms, p99=210ms, tkn/s=21.3, QA_acc=83.9% (Δ=-3.0%) -> 1.36x p50 speedup BUT larger quality loss
- INT8 (stable_int8): p50=82ms, p99=225ms, tkn/s=18.9, QA_acc=85.6% (Δ=-1.3%) -> less speedup, better quality
- FP8: p50=68ms, p99=200ms, tkn/s=22.0, QA_acc=86.2% (Δ=-0.7%) -> 1.4x p50 speedup

anya: A100 (ap-southeast) — noisier due to host kernel version mismatch
- FP16: p50=102ms, p99=260ms, QA_acc=86.9%
- INT8 (fast_int8_v2): p50=68ms, p99=230ms, QA_acc=82.4% (Δ=-4.5%) -> artifacts on numeric-heavy prompts
- FP8: p50=75ms, p99=210ms, QA_acc=85.9%

sylvie: Two quick interpretations: 1) H100 is the obvious INT8 win for small-batch; quality hit manageable (~1.8%). 2) A100 int8 behavior is kernel-sensitive — use stable_int8 on eu-west for less regression even if slower.

raj: Did you check kernel binary versions and cuBLAS/cuDNN? ap-southeast mismatch sounds like the known 2025-07 runtime issue.

anya: yes — ap-southeast had runtime 1.12.3, others 1.12.6. Re-ran stable_int8 on ap-southeast and QA_acc improved to 84.7% (was 82.4%). Still worse than eu-west.

matt: Any p99 catastrophes for production traffic? small-batch is p99 sensitive.

anya: p99s increased with INT8 across the board (tail queues) — H100 p99 still okay for our SLA (210ms). A100 p99 with fast_int8_v2 sometimes hits 400ms under bursty load.

anya: Kernel notes:
- H100: fast_int8_v2 uses tensor-core packing + mixed-kernel -> best perf/quality tradeoff here.
- A100: fast_int8_v2 triggers a quant clipping path that amplifies LM tokenization edge cases -> quality drop. stable_int8 uses slower accumulator path but safer.

anya: config suggestion to try on staging:
```json
{
  "policy": [
    {"region":"us-west","gpu":"h100","qprofile":"int8_fast","min_slo_ms":120},
    {"region":"eu-west","gpu":"a100","qprofile":"fp8_default","min_slo_ms":150},
    {"region":"ap-southeast","gpu":"a100","qprofile":"stable_int8","min_slo_ms":160}
  ]
}
```

matt: +1 for region+gpu policy. Also add a fallback to fp16 when QA_acc drop >1.5% on rolling eval.

sylvie: How about automated canary: route 5% traffic to int8_fast on H100, monitor QA_acc on prompt-suite, auto-rollback on ΔQA<-1.2% or p99>300ms.

raj: We should add kernel version gating to deployment pipeline. If runtime <1.12.6, block fast_int8.

infra-bot: deploy-check: runtime versions in ap-southeast: [1.12.3], eu-west: [1.12.6], us-west: [1.12.6]. Gate rule created: #PR-4579.

anya: TL;DR takeaways:
- H100: INT8 (fast_int8_v2) is a strong small-batch perf win (~2x p50) with ~1.5-2% QA hit — acceptable for some latency-sensitive paths with eval gating.
- A100: FP8 gives consistent moderate perf (~1.4x) with small quality cost (~<1%); INT8 behavior depends on kernel version — use stable_int8 or avoid unless validated.
- Region/runtime mismatches explain odd regressions; add kernel gating.

matt: Action items:
- anya: run a 24h canary on H100 int8_fast @5% traffic (start tomorrow) — include prompt-suite and latency p99 alarms. (owner=anya)
- raj: add runtime gate to infra pipeline (owner=raj)
- sylvie: prepare rollout doc + auto-rollback thresholds (owner=sylvie)

anya: starting canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC. Will post results and CSV of raw numbers in this thread.

matt: thanks — great concise summary. :rocket:
